election_dates.primarySnippet: N.J.S.A. 19:2-1: Primary elections for delegates and alternates to national conventions of political parties and for the general election shall be held in each year on the Tuesday next after the first Monday in June between the hours of 6:00 A.M. and 8:00 P.M., Standard Time.
election_dates.generalSnippet: N.J.S.A. 19:2-3: General and special elections. The general election shall be held on the Tuesday next after the first Monday in November in each year.

state_background_check.value: No — New Jersey has no blanket felony-disqualification rule for elective office; its only relevant statute permanently bars someone from future office only if they were convicted of an offense that involved or touched the specific state or local office they already held, and by its own text that bar reaches only offices "under this State or any of its administrative or political subdivisions," not federal office
state_background_check.snippet: N.J.S.A. 2C:51-2(d): "In addition to the punishment prescribed for the offense, and the forfeiture set forth in subsection a. of N.J.S.2C:51-2, any person convicted of an offense involving or touching on his public office, position or employment shall be forever disqualified from holding any office or position of honor, trust or profit under this State or any of its administrative or political subdivisions."

bio_summary.value: South Jersey Born and Raised. Lived my 31 years in different parts of South Jersey. I am running for something bigger than myself. I am running for change. For hope. I came from a section 8 neighborhood as a child and I was often dismissed of opportunity or told I would be a bad influence. I am running as an underdog and to be an inspiration to those who like myself come from an unhoused or poor past riddled with obstacles. My life was paused for many years because of a serious back injury and now that I am on the tail-end of my recovery, I can no longer sit by as I see the district I love neglected by corporate democrats and by republican representatives.

platform.value: Focus on lowering the cost of living by addressing hidden fees and reducing taxes on working families, with a fair tax system that holds corporations and the wealthiest accountable.
platform.snippet: To grow the middle class, we must have a fair tax system that holds corporations and the wealthiest accountable. I will focus on lowering the cost of living by addressing hidden fees and reducing taxes on working families.

platform.value: Increase federal funding for affordable housing development in South Jersey and support first-time homebuyer assistance programs.
platform.snippet: I will increase federal funding for affordable housing development in South Jersey and support first-time homebuyer assistance programs.

platform.value: Push for federal incentives for energy-efficient homes and businesses, federal investment in coastal resiliency, wetland and dune restoration, and infrastructure to protect communities, and support initiatives for clean air and clean water.
platform.snippet: We need to utilize all of our resources to harness renewable energy. I will push for federal incentives for energy-efficient homes and businesses to protect our environment and save money for working families. We need federal investment in coastal resiliency, wetland and dune restoration, and infrastructure to protect our communities. I will fight to preserve South Jersey's beaches, wetlands, and fishing industry. I will support initiatives for clean air and clean water.

platform.value: Push for public financing of elections, ban members of Congress from trading stocks, and demand full transparency in political spending.
platform.snippet: We need public financing of elections so that candidates answer to the people, not to billionaires and corporate PACs. I will push to ban members of Congress from trading stocks, because no elected official should be profiting from the decisions they make. We need full transparency in political spending so voters know exactly who is funding campaigns.

platform.value: Strongly oppose any cuts or privatization of Social Security, and fight to strengthen it for future generations.

platform.value: Fight to expand Medicare to include dental, vision, and hearing care, protect Medicaid, push to expand Medicare's power to negotiate drug prices, expand mental health services for all Americans, and work toward a Medicare for All system funded by fairer corporate taxes.
platform.snippet: I will fight to expand Medicare to include dental, vision, and hearing care, protect Medicaid, and support programs that help seniors. Healthcare is a human right, not a privilege reserved only for those who can afford it. Corporate greed is driving up costs. I will push to expand Medicare's power to negotiate drug prices, expand mental health services for all Americans, and work toward a Medicare for All system funded by fairer corporate taxes.

bio_summary.value: I am a lifelong resident of South Jersey I earned a Bachelor’s degree from Mount St. Mary’s University, where I was class president and a student athlete. I went on to earn an MBA from Saint Joseph’s University. I have been on the Cape May City Council for eight years, Mayor for six, elected three times. I have not raised taxes in the last seven years and we have built a new library and Fire House and we are in the process of building a new Police Station and upgrading our Lifeguard Headquarters to increase space for female lifeguards. Outside of being Mayor I helped found and build the Harriet Tubman Museum and the Cape May Point Arts and Science Center.

bio_summary.value: Jefferson H. Van Drew [ 1 ] (born February 23, 1953) [ 2 ] is an American politician serving as the U.S. representative for New Jersey's 2nd congressional district since 2019. He was first elected as a Democrat and later switched to the Republican Party in 2020. Before being elected to Congress, Van Drew held several public offices, including fire commissioner, township committee member, Mayor of Dennis Township, New Jersey , and Cape May County Freeholder . He represented New Jersey's 1st legislative district in the New Jersey General Assembly from 2002 to 2008, and represented the same district in the New Jersey Senate from 2008 to 2018.
